title: Problems with two right-angled triangles
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:54Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point covers finding sides and angles in a single right-angled triangle, while the new point needs a side from a first triangle to be carried into a second triangle, which is a different skill.

draft.title: Problems with two right-angled triangles
card: Some problems hide two right-angled triangles that share a side. Draw both and mark the shared side.
Use the triangle with enough information first. Find the shared side there, using a trigonometric ratio or Pythagoras' theorem.
Then use that side in the second triangle to find what the problem asks for.

Example: a flagpole stands on a building. From a point 30 m from the base, the angle up to the bottom of the pole is 45° and to the top is 60°. The building is 30 × tan 45° = 30 m high. The top is 30 × tan 60° = 52.0 m high. The pole is 52.0 − 30 = 22.0 m long.
draft.remember: Solve the triangle you can, then pass its shared side to the next.

a.q: Triangles ABD and CBD both have a right angle at D and share side BD. In triangle ABD, AB = 10 m and angle A = 30°. In triangle CBD, CD = 12 m. What is BC?
a.why: In triangle ABD, BD = 10 × sin 30° = 5 m. Then BC = √(5² + 12²) = 13 m. 15.6 m is tempting, but it comes from using 10 instead of the shared side 5.
a.clue: Find BD first, then use it in the second triangle.

b.q: Hasan stands in Hobart, 50 m from the base of a building with a radio mast on its roof. The angle up to the bottom of the mast is 45° and to the top is 60°. How long is the mast?
b.why: The building is 50 × tan 45° = 50 m high. The top of the mast is 50 × tan 60° = 86.6 m high. The mast is the difference: 86.6 − 50 = 36.6 m. 86.6 m is tempting, but that is the height of the top, not the mast.
b.clue: The mast is the difference between two heights.

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers check out (BD = 5 m so BC = 13 m; the mast is 86.6 − 50 = 36.6 m), and the card's example is correct.
